title: Micro-batch greedy merger with KV-priority and spillback controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a micro-batch formation heuristic for streaming chat completions that greedily merges near-term candidate turns while prioritizing sessions with hot KV cache entries and respecting GPU memory budgets. The goal is to reduce per-token overhead from repeated KV loads and to increase overall throughput without violating latency SLOs for interactive users. This ticket covers: metric design, algorithm prototype in the runtime planner, simulated evaluation against production traffic traces, a low-risk rollout plan with abort/spillback controls, and a follow-up observability dashboard.
background: Current continuous batching merges incoming tokens into micro-batches based primarily on arrival time and priority score. However, we observe high variance in latency during KV cache pressure: sessions that would benefit from coalescing are often separated because the planner avoids merging when estimated KV load increases GPU memory usage. Additionally, expensive KV restores for cold sessions dominate tail latency. We need a heuristic that explicitly accounts for KV-hotness and GPU occupancy to safely increase effective batching while providing spillback when memory pressure threatens SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Heuristic implemented in planner and can be toggled per-route via console flags
End-to-end simulation shows >=7% token-cost reduction on sampled chat traces with <=5% 99th-percentile latency regression
Runtime exposes metrics: kv_merge_accept_rate, kv_spillbacks, gpu_mem_margin, microbatch_size_distribution
Automated canary rollout with abort-on-increase for error-rate or latency regression defined in rollout policy
Documentation (Confluence) describing algorithm and trade-offs and a follow-up runbook for incidents
design_notes: Key idea: compute a KV-priority score for each pending session based on 'estimated KV delta' (how many new KV pages would need to be materialized if merged) and 'kv_staleness' (time since last KV access). Merge candidates are ranked by combined score = merge_benefit / (1 + kv_delta_weight * estimated_kv_delta) where merge_benefit captures token amortization and deadline slack. We add an explicit GPU_mem_margin check: predicted_gpu_usage + kv_estimated_bytes <= gpu_soft_limit * spill_tolerance. If the check fails, mark candidate for spillback (send to alternate lower-cost path or force early flush). The heuristic is intentionally greedy to keep decision latency sub-ms.
tradeoffs: Aggressive merging increases token throughput but risks KV thrashing; we mitigate with kv_staleness and spillback thresholds
Estimating kv_estimated_bytes is approximate — we favor conservative over-approximation to avoid OOMs, which can reduce merge opportunities
Adding these calculations increases planner CPU cost slightly (microseconds per decision); acceptable versus GPU memory and token-cost gains
implementation_plan: Prototype scoring function in planner simulation harness (local) using sampled production traces
Add kv metadata propagation to request envelope: last_kv_seq, estimated_kv_pages, last_kv_access_time
Implement greedy merge + gpu_mem_margin gating in runtime planner with feature flag
Add spillback hooks: route to low-memory local pool or force immediate flush
End-to-end sim and perf regression on canary worker pool
Gradual rollout with automated abort rules and dashboarding
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and observability. Agreed on metric set and simulated traces to use (7 days of edge-prod chat traffic).

2026-02-18: Prototype scoring function added to planner-sim harness (branch: feat/sim-kv-priority). Initial sim shows 9% token reduction but 8% 99p latency regression when memory over-approx is disabled.
2026-02-24: Added conservative kv_estimated_bytes heuristic and gpu_soft_limit gating. Regression on sim reduced to 3.5% 99p latency while token savings stayed at 6.3%.
2026-03-02: Implemented spillback path in runtime (branch: feat/spillback-route). Spillbacks are routed to dedicated low-memory workers with smaller KV footprints.
2026-03-08: Integration tests green. Metrics emitting kv_merge_accept_rate and kv_spillbacks. Observability dashboard prototype MVP available: /dashboards/kv-batching.html
2026-03-12: Started internal canary on 5% of hosted traffic in us-west-2. Monitoring for 99p latency, error-rate, and gpu_mem_margin. No aborts so far; early telemetry matches sim projections.
decisions: Use greedy one-shot merge rather than multi-pass optimization to keep planner latency under 500us
Conservative kv_estimated_bytes computation based on page-aligned sizes and include model-specific overhead constants
Spillback implemented as routing to a low-memory pool rather than immediate rejection to preserve availability
Expose per-route toggle in Console and default to off for enterprise customers with strict SLOs
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Underestimated KV overhead could lead to elevated GPU memory pressure -> Mitigation: conservative estimates + OOM guards and immediate spillback
Risk: Planner CPU cost adds up under very high qps -> Mitigation: micro-optimizations and sampling of low-priority traffic
Risk: Spillback increases tail latency for some sessions -> Mitigation: configurable spill_tolerance thresholds and fallback to alternate model variant
observability_and_metrics: kv_merge_accept_rate: proportion of merge proposals accepted
kv_spillbacks: count of spillback events per minute
microbatch_size_distribution: histogram of formed micro-batch sizes
kv_estimated_bytes_histogram: distribution of estimated per-merge KV bytes
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring function edge-cases (cold session, hot session, deadline tightness)
Simulation with 7-day production trace comparing baseline vs new heuristic
Stress test for planner CPU overhead at 2x peak QPS
Canary rollout on 5% then 25% then 100% with abort thresholds on 99p latency and error-rate
Runbook dry-run with SREs for spillback and abort scenarios
next_steps: Monitor canary for 7 days and collect kv_merge_accept_rate and gpu_mem_margin signals
Iterate on kv_estimated_bytes constants per model family (gpt-like vs encoder-only)
Prepare runbook and add rollback playbook to Console rollout config
Schedule Design review with PM and DS for user-visible trade-offs (latency vs cost)
